training_data.user_story: US1 - Analyze Black Friday Campaign ROI

messages.content: What were the top 3 performing ads in our Black Friday Tread Campaign by click-through rate?

Based on the Black Friday Tread Campaign data, the top 3 ads by CTR were:
1. 'Fall Into Fitness' video ad – 4.8% CTR (288,000 clicks on 6M impressions)
2. 'Ride With Us' carousel – 3.9% CTR
3. 'Your Goals, Our Classes' static – 3.2% CTR

Video formats consistently outperformed static assets across the 28–45 age bracket. I recommend shifting 15–20% of the static budget toward video for the next campaign cycle.

training_data.user_story: US1 - Analyze Black Friday Campaign ROI

messages.content: What was the overall ROI on the Black Friday Tread campaign and how much did we spend?

The Black Friday Tread Campaign generated a 2,330% ROI. Total spend was $210,000 against $5,103,000 in attributed revenue (3,402 conversions at an average order value of ~$1,499). The cost-per-acquisition was $61.73, well below the $120 target. The campaign was highly efficient — especially on Meta video placements.
What type of content gets the most shares among our members?

Based on the last 6 months of engagement data across 284 posts, HIIT Cycling content leads with an 18% engagement rate and 42,000 average shares per post. Beginner Yoga content follows at 15% engagement (31,000 shares), and Mental Wellness/Meditation content rounds out the top 3 at 13% (27,000 shares). Short-form video outperforms all other formats — posts under 60 seconds see 2.3x the shares of static images.
Suggest 3 content themes for our Q2 social media calendar based on what's worked recently.

Based on engagement trends, here are 3 recommended Q2 themes:

1. **Spring Reset** – Capitalize on the seasonal motivation shift in April. Feature beginner-friendly cycling and yoga for returning members. Expected 12–15% engagement lift based on similar spring 2023 content.

2. **Consistency Challenge** – Gamified streak content (e.g., 30-day challenges) targeting lapsed members. This drove the highest re-engagement rate of any campaign type last year at 22%.

3. **Outdoor x Indoor** – Cross-promote Peloton's outdoor running and walking app content as warmer weather arrives, bridging app-only and equipment members.
How is Peloton's membership growth comparing to NordicTrack and Echelon?

Here is the YoY membership growth comparison as of 2024:

| Brand        | 2022        | 2023        | 2024        | YoY 2024 |
|--------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|----------|
| Peloton      | 6.7M        | 6.1M        | 5.9M        | -3.3%    |
| NordicTrack  | 2.1M        | 2.4M        | 2.65M       | +10.4%   |
| Echelon      | 900K        | 1.05M       | 1.18M       | +12.4%   |

While Peloton retains the largest subscriber base, NordicTrack and Echelon are growing faster. Peloton's decline is linked to post-pandemic normalization and price sensitivity. Recommendation: prioritize retention programs and a lower-cost tier to compete on value.
What content strategies are our competitors using to grow their membership?

Based on publicly available data: NordicTrack has been aggressively marketing lower price points ($999 iFIT bike) and bundling free 12-month memberships with equipment purchases, reducing the upfront commitment barrier. Echelon focuses on value positioning ($500–$800 bikes) and targets fitness-curious users who haven't committed to premium equipment. Both brands have increased YouTube and TikTok short-form content spend by an estimated 40% YoY. Peloton's differentiation remains instructor brand equity and community — leaning further into instructor-led content and live class FOMO could reinforce this advantage.
